title: 2006 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 7
statement: Suppose we have an octagon with all angles of \(135^{\circ}\), and consecutive sides of alternating length 1 and \(\sqrt{2}\). We draw all its sides and diagonals. Into how many regions do the segments divide the octagon? (No proof is necessary.)

solutions.text: The easiest way to see the answer is to view the octagon as five unit squares in a cross arrangement, with four half-squares wedged at the corners. The center square is divided into 8 regions. The other 4 squares are each divided into 15 regions. The 4 half-squares are each divided into 4 regions. The answer is thus \(8+4 \times 15+4 \times 4=84\).
